verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's first-party docs describe faceting as filters that also return aggregated counts per field value. They explicitly cite e-commerce navigation by brand, color, size and price range with counts per option (e.g. "Color: Red (12), Blue (8)"), and a dedicated facet-search endpoint for large facet lists. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that facet distributions and results come back in one search request, detail on range-facet statistics (min/max) for numeric ranges, and independent hands-on corroboration of faceted navigation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build faceted navigation — filters with live counts across categories, ranges, and attributes — from a single query

citations.quote: E-commerce faceted navigation: Let shoppers narrow products by brand, color, size, and price range while displaying counts for each option.
Faceting returns aggregated counts for field values, powering category navigation in your UI
Facets are filters that also return distribution data. Use them together to build interactive, ecommerce-style navigation.
Filters, ranges, and refinements that turn a long list of results into the right answer.
